A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Starve to Perceive research and contain complete, readable main text and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training-stage ablations, efficiency measurements, a qualitative comparison, and an appendix budget sweep.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results, including Tables 1–5 and the training-dynamics and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.4 and Listing 1 retain the same budgeted cropping procedure, resolution-conditioned budget, budget-aware SFT, and reinforcement learning with answer-correctness rewards. No architecture, objective, or algorithmic step changes.

E1.justification: Training sources and task coverage remain unchanged. Both evaluate HR-Bench, V* Bench, VisualProbe, MME-RealWorld-Lite, RealWorldQA, and TreeBench, including the same constrained, unconstrained, and budget-sweep scenarios.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, LLaVA-OneVision, PixelReasoner, DeepEyes, ChainOfFocus, Mini-o3, Qwen2.5-VL, and the same training-stage variants. Comparator membership in the ablation, efficiency, and appendix budget-sweep comparisons is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 retains greedy decoding, a three-turn evaluation limit, a 30k-token context limit, and constrained evaluation at B=256. Training settings, data filtering, sample counts, and the four appendix sweep budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the trajectory-controlled SFT ablation, training-stage comparisons and dynamics in Section 3.3, Appendix C's qualitative case study, and Appendix D's budget sensitivity analysis. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Run and seed disclosures and statistical reporting practices are unchanged. Benchmark tables continue to report point estimates without confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figures 2–4 retain their numerical and qualitative results. For example, the model's overall scores remain 64.59 unconstrained and 52.35 constrained, and Table 5's gains remain +1.38, +0.81, +0.50, and +0.60.

T1.justification: The information-bottleneck reasoning, interaction definitions, and Equations (1)–(5) are unchanged. Appendix coordinate transformations and mathematical descriptions are also retained; no proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the claim that bandwidth constraints make active perception the 'only viable strategy' to 'strongly incentivizing' it. The central method, transfer, accuracy, and efficiency claims remain, and stronger necessity language persists in the body and conclusion.

C2.justification: The contribution paragraph changes its interpretation of robustness from distinguishing grounded reasoning from tool-use mimicry to promoting grounding and mitigating mimicry. This is a limited qualification of the evidential interpretation; the detailed results discussion and Appendix A limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a repository link in the abstract and promises future public availability of code and data; v1 provides no such pointer. This adds access information without establishing an actual release. Implementation details and appendix prompts are unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix C removes the in-text citation cluster [29–31,33–35,44,45], although those bibliography entries remain. The main related-work discussion is unchanged. Reference 35's revised title and publication information concern the same work, rather than a newly introduced reference.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the abstract and contribution paragraph, the added resource sentence, corresponding-author identification, and bibliographic metadata. Section order, narrative organization, and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds running author/title headers and page numbers, removes bibliography back-references, and modestly reflows the opening and references. All four figures and five tables retain their displays, captions, and content.

improvement.justification: The abstract's more cautious incentive claim better fits Section 3.3's evidence that constrained RL without SFT can still collapse. The planned code/data pointer also improves resource discoverability. These are limited gains: experimental support is unchanged, stronger necessity wording remains elsewhere, and the PDFs do not establish actual resource availability.
